title: Plan Tonight's own #1 pick cannot be turned into a sequence: "no usable imaging window" for every non-circumpolar target
what_happened: With a valid site (40.0N, -75.0W) and an active equipment profile, the Tonight screen's card says "M92 — Peak alt: 84° — Hours up: 5.3 h — Excellent peak altitude (84°) ... 5.3 hours above minimum altitude". Clicking the single primary CTA "Image this target tonight" fails with the red error: 'Target "M92" has no usable imaging window between 2026-08-01T22:01:44.882 and 2026-08-02T04:11:18.515 at min altitude 30°.' The identical failure occurs from Plan Tonight → Recommendation → "Review in Sequencer" for M92 (score 77, the app's top pick) and for M31 (score 63). A circumpolar target (NGC6015, dec +62.3) succeeds and loads 261 frames / 3h59m into the sequencer, which bounds the bug: any target with a finite rise/set at the site is blocked. At lat 40 that is essentially the whole imaging sky (M31, M42, M27, M13, the Veil...).
expected: M92 is above 30° for 308 of the 370 minutes inside that exact window (astropy, 1-min grid, lat 40 lon -75, 2026-08-01). The builder should produce a sequence, or the card must not claim 5.3 usable hours. A screen whose entire purpose is pick -> sequence must not fail on its own default pick.
repro: 1. Settings > Location: lat 40, lon -75, elev 100. 2. Create an equipment profile (sim camera + sim mount, 600mm/120mm/3.76um). 3. Dashboard > "Image tonight" > click "Image this target tonight". 4. Also: Plan Tonight > Recommendation > "Review in Sequencer" on the hero card (M92) and on a searched M31. 5. Search NGC6015 and click "Review in Sequencer" -> succeeds.
proposed_fix: calculateObjectVisibility searches a noon-to-noon window anchored on the night MIDPOINT date (target_scoring.dart:404-413 passes nightMid, which is after local midnight), so the rise/set pair it returns describes a 24h day that does not bracket tonight's dark window: for M92 the returned rise is the NEXT day's 12:01, for M31 the returned set is the PREVIOUS afternoon's 14:13. _usableTargetWindow then clips [22:01, 04:11] with those and gets an empty interval. Either anchor calculateObjectVisibility on the interval start (windowStart) rather than the midpoint, or make _usableTargetWindow day-aware: if the target's altitude at intervalStart already exceeds minAltitude, do not clip with riseTime; if it exceeds it at intervalEnd, do not clip with setTime. A cheap regression test: assert buildSingleTargetSequence succeeds for a dec=+41 target at lat=40 on any date.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end-to-end on a fresh profile (site 40.0N/-75.0W, profile 'My First Rig' = sim camera + sim mount, 600mm/120mm/3.76um, no filter wheel). At 12:11 local the Tonight screen's own TONIGHT'S PICK was M92 ('Peak alt: 84 deg', 'Hours up: 5.3 h', '5.3 hours above minimum altitude'); clicking the single CTA 'Image this target tonight' produced the red error verbatim: Target "M92" has no usable imaging window between 2026-08-01T22:01:44.882 and 2026-08-02T04:11:18.515 at min altitude 30 deg. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-69-tonightfail.png). Same failure from Plan Tonight > Recommendation on the hero card's 'Review in Sequencer' (pv-67-crop.png) and on the M92 candidate card (pv-35b.png). Control confirmed: the circumpolar NGC6015 (dec +62.3) built a sequence fine and only failed downstream on device-connection validation (pv-28-built.png). Mechanism verified in source: target_scoring.dart:404-413 passes date: nightMid (post-midnight, i.e. Aug 2) to AstronomyCalculations.calculateObjectVisibility, which anchors its scan at DateTime(y,m,d,12) (astronomy_calculations.dart:1024) => the returned riseTime for M92 is Aug 2 12:01 (the card's own chart footer prints 'Rise: 12:01'), which sequence_emitter.dart:144-146 then uses as usableStart, so usableStart (Aug 2 12:01) is not before usableEnd (Aug 2 04:11) and _usableTargetWindow returns null (smart_night_service.dart:697-711 throws). Error string matches the source exactly. P0 stands: the app's headline one-tap path fails for every target with a finite rise/set at mid latitudes.

title: Dashboard SAFETY card shows a green "Safe" badge while reporting it has no data, at the same moment an app-wide red "Weather Critical" banner is up
what_happened: Dashboard right rail: SAFETY panel renders a green check badge reading "Safe", with body rows 'Data: Unavailable', 'As of 10:58:33', an amber inline alert 'No weather data sources available' and the line 'Weather safety is off — conditions are not being checked'. In the same session the app-wide banner reads 'Weather Critical / Weather safety is off — conditions are not being checked', and the Weather screen reports 'Cloud Cover 93% Overcast' with a Critical card 'Heavy cloud cover overhead (93% density) - consider pausing'. So one surface says Safe (green), one says Critical (red), about the same subject at the same time, and the Safe verdict is asserted from admittedly absent data.
expected: A safety verdict must never be green when the monitor is off or the data is unavailable. Show 'Not monitored' / 'Unknown' in a neutral or amber state. And the app-wide banner should not use the word 'Critical' for a configuration state (safety disabled) — that is the same word used for the genuine 93%-cloud alert, which trains the user to ignore both.
repro: 1. Set a location, connect the sim camera+mount profile, do not connect a weather/safety device. 2. Dashboard -> read the SAFETY card. 3. Weather -> scroll to the Critical card and Safety Status card. 4. Compare with the persistent top banner.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-84-restart.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-91-tonight.png (SAFETY = green "Safe", Data: Unavailable / Weather API, 'No weather data sources available'); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-88-weather4.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-89-weather5.png (Critical, 93% overcast, 'Not monitoring')
where: Dashboard safety card (rendered on /dashboard right rail); weather banner severity is driven by the disabled state of Settings > Automation & Safety > Weather Safety > 'Enable weather safety' (default off, screenshot planning-90)
proposed_fix: Make the badge tri-state: Safe (monitored and safe) / Unsafe / Not monitored (grey). Never map 'monitoring disabled' or 'no data' onto Safe. Downgrade the persistent banner for the disabled-monitor case from Critical to an informational one-time notice with a 'Turn on weather safety' action, and reserve Critical for an actual unsafe reading.
verdict_reasoning: Headline CONFIRMED and reproduced: with sim camera+mount connected and no weather/safety device, the Dashboard right rail renders SAFETY with a green check badge reading 'Safe' above 'Data: Unavailable', 'As of 11:55:29', the amber inline alert 'No weather data sources available' and 'Weather safety is off - conditions are not being checked' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-45-safety.png). Code anchors it: weather_safety_provider.dart:662-671 sets finalStatus = WeatherSafetyStatus.safe whenever weatherSafetyEnabled is false, and run_dashboard/weather_safety_card.dart:21-22 maps that straight to ('Safe', colors.success, check) with no tri-state for monitoringEnabled==false or dataSource==unavailable. The Weather screen in the same session is honest ('Safety Status: Not monitoring - weather safety is off'), so the two surfaces do contradict each other. SUB-CLAIM REFUTED: the app-wide banner does not use 'Critical' for the configuration state. weather_alert_banner.dart:57-60 gates the banner on currentAlertLevel (warning/critical) alone, and _getTitle() at :140-148 derives 'Weather Critical' from that level - i.e. from the reporter's genuine 93%-cloud alert. What is actually wrong is that the banner's MESSAGE is actions.reason, which the disabled branch overwrites with the 'safety is off' text - a mismatch, but the opposite of the diagnosis, so the proposed 'downgrade the disabled-monitor banner from Critical' fix targets a cause that does not exist. My session had 5% cloud so no banner appeared at all. P1 retained for the green-Safe-with-no-data badge.
